newsitem.title: USA: Viacom to take Q2 Blockbuster charge.
newsitem.headline: Viacom to take Q2 Blockbuster charge.

text.p: Viacom Inc said Monday it would take a second quarter charge of about $300 million related to its troubled Blockbuster Entertainment unit.
Viacom said the charge was primarily related to reducing the carrying value of excess inventory and the closing of underperforming stores in certain international markets.
A spokesman said no U.S. stores would be closed.
Viacom said its Blockbuster revenues and EBITDA -- earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization -- would be below analysts's estimates in the second quarter.
Viacom said Blockbuster second quarter revenues would range from $880 million to $900 million, while EBITDA before charges would be in the range of $40 to $50 million.
Viacom said Blockbuster revenues were being hurt by continued softness in the domestic video rential industry and "disruptions" from the unit's headquarters move to Dallas from Fort Lauderdale, Fla.
It also cited the "negative impact" from its recently discontinued "One World, One Word," ad campaign, and the impact of the change in focus from video rental to an expanded product mix in stores.
Viacom said EBITDA would be hurt by cost pressures stemming from new store development, and from buying too many videotapes and other products, resulting in excess inventory.

Viacom said that if a negative same-store sales trend continued in the second half of this year, revenue shortfalls could result in full-year Blockbuster EBITDA ranging from $400-$500 million, before charges.
Viacom said that apart from Blockbuster, the company "continues to perform well." Viacom will report second quarter results in early August.
Viacom cited several steps taken to address Blockbuster's problems.

It named John Antioco, who ran former PepsiCo Inc's Taco Bell unit, to run the video renter last month. It has shifted the advertising focus back to the slogan "Make it a Blockbuster Night," and a new campaign is being developed.

Viacom said the interim distribution system is being improved and the new distribution center, which it expects will result in "significant efficiencies," is on target to begin operating early next year.

It said it expects to boost Blockbuster's market share, strengthen marketing and promotion, improve store site selection, better target tape purchases and have a renewed emphasis on operational efficiency and customer service.
